A1. Bound exists and is validated. docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md section "Registration and resolution": "Establish max input/output sizes, execution deadlines, memory/event quotas and secret redaction." -> new CapabilityRegistry({maxInFlight: 0}), ({maxInFlight: 1.5}) and ({maxInFlight: -1}) throw CapabilityError category "validation" with message "Invalid capability limit maxInFlight." (the existing limit-validation path); a registry constructed without the option uses the exported constant CAPABILITY_MAX_IN_FLIGHT and registry.admission().maxInFlight equals that constant (the test imports the constant; no literal).

A2. FIFO wait, not refusal, while a slot will free. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Runtime and host requirements": "Streaming bounded by max in-flight node calls, backend admission and configured quota." -> with {maxInFlight: 1} and a provider whose invoke resolves only when the test releases it, three concurrent invoke() calls reach provider.invoke one at a time in request order (release #1 -> #2 enters; release #2 -> #3 enters); provider.invoke call count is exactly 1 until the first release; all three callers resolve with their validated values; admission() reports inFlight 0, peakInFlight 1, admitted 3, refused 0 afterwards.

A3. Typed admission refusal, distinct from the transport deadline, provider never called. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md section "Workbench core types" (NodeCallResult): `{ kind: "rejected"; category: "validation" | "authorization" | "unavailable"; diagnostic: string }` and docs/workbench/06 section "Current experimental policy surface": "A deadline stops the caller's wait; it does not establish producer rollback." -> with {maxInFlight: 1, deadlineMs: 50} and the first call held open, a second invoke() rejects with CapabilityError category "unavailable" whose message contains "admission" and the bound; the provider was called exactly once (never for the second request); the message differs from the existing transport-deadline text ("exceeded its deadline"); a third call issued after the first is released succeeds (the refusal left no stale queue state).

A4. Cancellation while queued. docs/workbench/06 section "InvocationContext": "cancellation signal for current wait" -> a queued call whose context.signal aborts rejects with CapabilityError category "transport" (the existing cancellation family), provider.invoke count unchanged, and admission().cancelledWhileQueued increments by one; the slot order of the remaining waiters is unchanged (the next waiter still enters when the running call settles).

A5. Slot held until the provider settles. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "State/event semantics" (via the registry's own deadline comment): a caller rejected by its transport deadline while the provider promise is still pending leaves admission().inFlight at 1 until the provider promise settles; a new call with {maxInFlight: 1} during that window is admission-refused (A3 path) rather than dispatched alongside the hung provider; after the provider settles inFlight returns to 0. Uncertain-effect semantics of the existing deadline path are unchanged (no new "uncertain-effect" category minted here).

A6. Inspect mode shares the bound. docs/workbench/06 section "Optional inspect/observe" -> registry inspect-mode calls occupy the same slots as invoke-mode calls (one held inspect blocks a second invoke under {maxInFlight: 1} and vice versa), proven both directions.

A7. Never auto-retry. docs/workbench/06 section "Registration and resolution": "No generic auto-retry; producer-specific adapters alone may reconcile native logical identities." -> after an admission refusal or a queued cancellation the provider is never invoked later for that request (count asserted after all other calls settle and after one macrotask turn).

A8. Telemetry snapshot is counts only. docs/workbench/17 section "Operations telemetry": "Report actual: ... provider call outcomes ..." and "Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default." -> admission() returns an Object.isFrozen snapshot with exactly the keys maxInFlight, inFlight, peakInFlight, admitted, refused, cancelledWhileQueued, all safe integers; serialized it contains no capability id, provider name, input or output text (asserted against a fixture whose capability id and payload carry a unique marker).

A9. No production behaviour change elsewhere: src diff touches only src/workbench/capability-registry.ts; all existing registry/security/node-contract/curated-tool suites pass unchanged; biome clean; no any; no inline imports; no hot file touched.

description:
Gap (measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program 250c0af, groom seat g2 round 12): docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md section "Reader adapters" lists six producers. Claude (wb-6ze.3, closed), Forge (wb-6hb.2, closed), Furnace (wb-752.1, closed), HX (wb-6ze.7, in progress) and RF (wb-6ze.9, ready) each have an adapter bead; the row "Beads: supported work readiness and linkage, never reconstructed from heuristics alone" has none (bd census over open/closed/in_progress/blocked: no title or description mentions Beads, bd, work readiness or linkage). The landed Furnace observer already surfaces Beads identity without resolving it: FurnaceReading.source.beadsRunId (src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts:24 and :108) and FurnaceAttemptReference.workId (:18, :57), so the inspector can show a Furnace Attempt's work id but never what work it is, whether it is ready or blocked, or what it depends on; docs/workbench/02 WB-025 ("distinguishes Run/Work/Attempt") stays experimental. No Beads SDK is vendored (vendor/ holds forge, furnace and hyperunix tarballs only) and docs/workbench/07 section "Beads provider" forbids assuming one; the only integration contract available is the bd CLI JSON output, measured this round with bd version 1.1.0-rc.1 (2d9e4321c): `bd show <id> --json` prints an ARRAY of issue objects with keys acceptance_criteria, comment_count, created_at, created_by, dependencies, dependency_count, dependent_count, description, id, issue_type, notes, owner, parent, priority, spec_id, status, title, updated_at (plus closed_at and close_reason when closed); each dependencies[] entry carries id, title, status, issue_type, priority and dependency_type ('blocks' for a blocker this issue waits on, 'parent-child' for its parent, and other types such as 'discovered-from' or 'related'), plus description/notes text. Measured direction: wb-6ze.16 waits on wb-g1g.2 and its dependencies[] entry for wb-g1g.2 reads dependency_type 'blocks'.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/beads-observer.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-beads-observer.test.ts, modelled on the pure projector src/workbench/claude-topology.ts (projectClaudeTopology) and the injected client seam of src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts.

- export const BEADS_WORK_CONTRACT = 'beads.work.readiness/v1' (defined exactly once and consumed by identifier; wb-cax.8 single-carrier rule).
- export interface BeadsReadClient { show(id: string, call: { cwd: string; timeoutMs: number; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<{ exit: number; stdout: string; stderr: string }> } - injected; tests use a fake; the module never imports node:child_process (static source assertion in the test, like the wb-6ze.10 "SDK never imported" falsifier). A live bd tier is out of scope.
- export async function readBeadsWork(client: BeadsReadClient, options: { workId: string; workspaceRoot: string; scope: ObservationScope; limits: { maxDependencies: number; maxTitleChars: number; timeoutMs: number }; now: () => string }): Promise<BeadsWorkReading>. BeadsWorkReading = { contract; source: { provider: 'beads'; workId; workspaceRoot; ownership: 'external'; producer: 'bd'; producerVersion?: string (only when the seam measured it, never guessed) }; capturedAt; observedAt; freshness: 'current'; completeness: 'complete' | 'partial'; work: { status: string; issueType: string; priority: number; parent?: string; closedAt?: string; closeReasonPresent: boolean }; dependencies: { offered: number; returned: number; truncated: boolean; items: { id: string; dependencyType: string; status: string }[] }; unmappedDependencyTypes: Record<string, number> }.
  - Identity: the seam runs with cwd = workspaceRoot; options.scope.workspace must equal workspaceRoot (host-bound) else CapabilityError('authorization'). A non-zero exit, non-JSON stdout, a non-array or empty array, or a first element whose id differs from workId is CapabilityError('unavailable') - a missing store or a foreign record is refused, never an empty or borrowed readiness. An aborted signal is CapabilityError('transport').
  - Retention: only title (bounded to maxTitleChars, through redactWorkbenchText and stripUnsafeText imported from src/workbench/redaction.ts - do not edit) and the enumerated scalar fields are retained; description, notes, acceptance_criteria and close_reason text are never copied (closeReasonPresent is a boolean). dependencies[] is cut at maxDependencies with offered/returned/truncated and completeness 'partial'.
- export function projectBeadsWork(reading: BeadsWorkReading, scope: ObservationScope): { snapshot: NativeSnapshot; relations: Parameters<ObservationProjection['relate']>[0][]; truncated: boolean }.
  - snapshot.source = { provider: 'beads', type: 'work', id: workId, scope: workspaceRoot }; kind 'beads.work.snapshot'; coverage from completeness; node.type 'group' when issueType is 'epic' else 'sdk-operation'; statusText is the native status string verbatim; statusTone: in_progress -> 'active'; open, blocked, deferred -> 'waiting'; closed -> 'unknown' (closure is a readiness fact, not a verified outcome: wb-6ze.12 is closed as a withdrawn duplicate); any unrecognized status -> 'unknown'. No evidenceRefs are invented.
  - relations: each dependencies[] entry with dependency_type 'blocks' -> { kind: 'dependency', from: the work ref, to: { provider: 'beads', type: 'work', id: entry.id, scope: workspaceRoot }, provenance: { source: 'beads', observedAt, nativeConfirmationRef: 'bd:show:<workId>' } } - from the dependent work to its blocker, the direction src/workbench/attention.ts:170 already reads dependency edges in; a 'parent-child' entry or the parent field -> ONE { kind: 'grouping', from: parent ref, to: work ref } edge (deduplicated when both name the same id); every other dependency_type -> counted in unmappedDependencyTypes and produces no edge (a native non-dependency link is never minted as a hypothesis or dependency). Ownership edges are never produced.

Red-first falsifiers in test/workbench-beads-observer.test.ts: (1) returned id != requested id -> 'unavailable', nothing projected; (2) exit != 0, malformed JSON or empty array -> 'unavailable', never an empty-ready work; (3) 'related' and 'discovered-from' entries -> zero edges and a count; (4) a closed work item never renders statusTone 'success'; (5) hostile title (ANSI, bidi, credential-shaped text) is sanitized and description/notes/close_reason never appear anywhere in the reading or snapshot (deep JSON string search); (6) dependencies beyond maxDependencies -> truncated true, offered vs returned honest, completeness 'partial'; (7) scope.workspace != workspaceRoot -> 'authorization'; (8) aborted signal -> 'transport'; (9) source assertion: the module imports nothing from node:child_process; (10) mutation proof: one single-point mutant per falsifier is killed.

Out of scope: a live bd tier (separate Forge command and bead), joining Furnace Attempt.workId to Beads inside furnace-observer.ts, Pi tool registration (src/index.ts is hot), dialog/inspector wiring (src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts is hot), editing src/workbench/observation.ts, src/workbench/redaction.ts, src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts or any file in the BOUNDARY hot set.

Specs: docs/workbench/09 (Observer mandate; Reader adapters; Relationships are typed and provenanced), docs/workbench/07 (Beads provider), docs/workbench/02 WB-025 and WB-037, docs/workbench/12 (Input and output hardening), docs/workbench/15 W13.

title: W22-K/docs-17: pure operations-telemetry report over the projection and supplied counters (active workflows with last-known-running+stale sub-count, Claude SDK sessions, provider call outcomes, event lag p50/p95 + clock caveat, dropped/late observations, projection size, visible rows, render p95, memory, SDK tokens, evidence coverage, ambiguous effects; each metric measured-with-source or unknown-with-reason, never default zero; counts and sanitized provider names only); wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at trunk 0ef5aeb, origin/workbench/implementation-program): docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Operations telemetry" requires "Report actual: active workflows, Claude SDK sessions, provider call outcomes, event lag, dropped/late observations, projection size, number of visible rows, UI render p95, memory, token use from SDK, native evidence coverage and ambiguous external effects. Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default." grep -rni 'telemetry' src/ returns one OpenTelemetry comment (src/index.ts:714); no module aggregates any of these twelve quantities. The inputs exist: ObservationProjection exposes query() (src/workbench/observation.ts:477), events() (:540, completeness "complete" | "partial-gap") and stats() (:558 -> {nodes, events, edges}); ObservedNode carries kind, presentation.statusTone, freshness, sourceConnectionState, evidenceRefs and nativeRef (:56-76); ObservationEvent carries sourceTimestamp? and observedAt (:12-28); ingest() returns "applied" | "duplicate" | "out-of-order" (:261) but retains no counters; CapabilityErrorCategory (src/workbench/capability-registry.ts:39) names the provider outcome categories; the Claude host computes per-call token usage (src/workbench/claude-host.ts:83-89) but publishes no aggregate. wb-6ze.4 (landed a4cd2cf) set the pattern this bead follows: a pure, caller-clocked, bounded selector over one projection page with measured-vs-unknown labelling. wb-752.2 (in progress) builds the workflow_observe reply and may surface this report later; wb-cax.10 (owner-held) covers the other docs/17 residual (lazy init). No bead covers operations telemetry.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/telemetry.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-telemetry.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const TELEMETRY_CONTRACT = "workbench.telemetry/v1"; export const TELEMETRY_CLOCK_CAVEAT (event lag compares producer sourceTimestamp with observedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled).
- export type TelemetryMetric<T> = { state: "measured"; value: T; source: "projection" | "supplied" } | { state: "unknown"; reason: "not-supplied" | "invalid-supplied" | "no-source-timestamps" | "no-events" }.
- export interface SuppliedCounters { providerCallOutcomes?: Readonly<Partial<Record<"returned" | CapabilityErrorCategory, number>>>; droppedObservations?: number; lateObservations?: number; visibleRows?: number; renderP95Ms?: number; heapUsedBytes?: number; sdkTokens?: number; claudeSessions?: number; uncertainEffects?: number } -- the host/dialog counts these (ingest results, provider outcomes, render timings, SDK usage) and passes them in; this bead defines the shape only.
- export function buildOperationsTelemetry(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "events" | "stats">, input: { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId?: string; now: string; limit?: number (default 100, max 100); eventLimit?: number (default 200, max 1000); supplied?: SuppliedCounters }): OperationsTelemetry -- a frozen report { contract; now; examined: { nodes; truncated; events; eventsTruncated; completeness: "complete" | "partial-gap" }; activeWorkflows: TelemetryMetric<{ active: number; lastKnownRunningStale: number }>; claudeSdkSessions: TelemetryMetric<number> (projection count of nodes with nativeRef.provider "claude-agent-sdk" and type "session"; a supplied claudeSessions is reported beside it with source "supplied", never merged); providerCallOutcomes: TelemetryMetric<Record<string, number>>; eventLag: TelemetryMetric<{ p50Ms; p95Ms; samples; unmeasured; providers: string[]; caveat: string }>; droppedObservations, lateObservations: TelemetryMetric<number>; projectionSize: TelemetryMetric<{ nodes; events; edges }>; visibleRows, renderP95Ms, heapUsedBytes, sdkTokens, uncertainEffects: TelemetryMetric<number>; nativeEvidenceCoverage: TelemetryMetric<{ withEvidence: number; examined: number }> }.
- Rules: projection-derived metrics come from ONE bounded projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit}) page and ONE bounded projection.events({scope, limit: eventLimit}) read; truncated and partial-gap flags are propagated into examined. activeWorkflows.active counts nodes with kind "workflow" and statusTone "active"; lastKnownRunningStale counts those with freshness !== "current" or sourceConnectionState "disconnected" (docs/09 § "Freshness and ambiguity" nuance). eventLag samples are observedAt minus sourceTimestamp in ms for events carrying both (negative samples clamp to 0 and are counted in unmeasured, as are events without sourceTimestamp); p50/p95 by nearest-rank over the sorted samples; providers = sorted distinct event.source.provider. Supplied metrics are measured only when the supplied value is a finite non-negative number (for the outcome record: every value finite non-negative), else unknown "not-supplied" / "invalid-supplied"; the report never defaults an absent counter to 0. now is the caller's clock (ISO-8601 with timezone; the module never calls Date.now); the projection is never mutated.
- Redaction: the report contains no node titles, status text, evidence ref strings, prompts, tool bodies or payload refs -- counts and provider names only; provider names pass redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText (src/workbench/redaction.ts) and are capped at 64 chars; JSON.stringify(report) stays under 8 KiB for the maximum page and the test asserts it.

Out of scope: host-side counting (ingest-result counters, provider outcome counters, render timings, SDK usage aggregation live in src/index.ts, the dialog and hosts -- HOT or owner wiring; this bead defines SuppliedCounters only), inspector header or workflow_observe surfacing (wb-752.2), process.memoryUsage or any node:* read inside the module, docs or TRACEABILITY edits.

acceptance_criteria:
All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, base 0ef5aeb or later per BOUNDARY.md).
1. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Operations telemetry": "Report actual: active workflows, Claude SDK sessions, provider call outcomes, event lag, dropped/late observations, projection size, number of visible rows, UI render p95, memory, token use from SDK, native evidence coverage and ambiguous external effects." -> the report type has exactly these twelve metric fields (plus contract, now, examined); a fixture projection with 3 workflow nodes (2 active, 1 success) and 2 "claude-agent-sdk"/"session" nodes yields activeWorkflows {active:2, lastKnownRunningStale:0}, claudeSdkSessions 2 and projectionSize equal to projection.stats(); every field is either {state:"measured", value, source} or {state:"unknown", reason} (type-level exhaustiveness plus a runtime walk over the report).
2. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Agent execution contracts": "If the installed SDK lacks a field, omit it; no invented zeros or fake IDs." -> with supplied undefined, providerCallOutcomes, droppedObservations, lateObservations, visibleRows, renderP95Ms, heapUsedBytes, sdkTokens and uncertainEffects are all {state:"unknown", reason:"not-supplied"}; JSON.stringify(report) contains no "value":0 for those fields; a supplied NaN, -1 or Infinity yields "invalid-supplied"; a supplied {returned:4, transport:1, "uncertain-effect":1} is measured with source "supplied" and every key preserved.
3. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Observation event envelope (proposal)": "SourceTimestamp does not establish a total order across providers." -> eventLag over events from providers "forge" and "furnace" reports samples, p50Ms, p95Ms, providers ["forge","furnace"] and caveat === TELEMETRY_CLOCK_CAVEAT; events without sourceTimestamp are counted in unmeasured and never sampled; a window with zero timestamped events is {state:"unknown", reason:"no-source-timestamps"} ("no-events" when the window is empty); an events() read returning completeness "partial-gap" sets examined.completeness "partial-gap".
4. docs/workbench/09 § "Freshness and ambiguity": "A disconnected Furnace event stream must not make a previously RUNNING node permanently authoritative RUNNING; it becomes last-known-running + stale. Pi tool summaries must communicate that nuance." -> after projection.disconnect("furnace") an active furnace workflow node is counted in both active and lastKnownRunningStale; after a real refresh() snapshot restores the node, lastKnownRunningStale returns to 0 while active is unchanged; reconnect() alone does not clear it.
5. docs/workbench/17 § "Operations telemetry": "Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default." with docs/workbench/09 § "Data retention and privacy": "Avoid raw prompts/tool bodies by default; store reference/short redacted preview" and docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Credential boundaries": "redact tokens from logs, UI, recordings and failure messages." -> with node titles "Bearer abc123 secret", status text containing "api_key":"xyz" and evidenceRefs ["claude-message:0000"], JSON.stringify(report) contains none of "Bearer", "abc123", "xyz", "api_key" or "claude-message"; a provider name "fur\x1b[31mnace​" appears sanitized; JSON.stringify(report).length < 8192 for a 100-node/1000-event page.
6. docs/workbench/09 § "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics." -> nativeEvidenceCoverage reports {withEvidence, examined} as two counts (no ratio or percentage is invented); a query page capped at limit 100 over 150 nodes reports examined.truncated true and the test asserts the coverage counts describe the examined page, not the projection.
7. Purity: buildOperationsTelemetry never calls Date.now (static grep of the module plus a Date.now spy), never mutates the projection (stats() and query() results identical before and after), returns deep-frozen output (Object.isFrozen on every nested object), and the module's import specifiers are limited to ./observation.js, ./capability-registry.js and ./redaction.js (static assertion).
Process: red-first (the new test fails before src/workbench/telemetry.ts exists); ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on touched files; no any; no inline imports; never weaken or delete existing tests; hot files untouched (BOUNDARY 08:58:33Z state listed in notes); `git diff <base>..HEAD -- src/ | grep -n 'workflow-script/v1'` returns nothing; base 0ef5aeb or later; forge run lint / typing / test green in the worktree.

The store and the EvidenceEntry/EvidenceContent types come from wb-g1g.1 (open); the three pure readers come from wb-6ze.10 (src/workbench/claude-evidence.ts), wb-6ze.8 (src/workbench/furnace-evidence.ts, in progress) and wb-6ze.11 (src/workbench/forge-evidence.ts). Without this slice the owner's dialog wiring has three readers and a store with no adapters between them.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/evidence-loaders.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-evidence-loaders.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const EVIDENCE_LOADER_ROWS: frozen table of exactly three rows {provider, requiredGrant, refKind}: {"claude-agent-sdk", "claude:transcript", "claude-message:<uuid>"}, {"furnace", "furnace:inspect", "native Attempt id listed on the owning run node"}, {"forge", "forge:inspect", "forge-operation:<operation_id>"} -- the docs/20 § "Producer mapping" table and nothing else.
- export function createEvidenceLoaders(input: { grants: () => readonly string[]; readers: { claude?: <landed claude-evidence.ts read function>; furnace?: <landed furnace-evidence.ts read function>; forge?: <landed forge-evidence.ts read function> }; owningFreshness: (scope: ObservationScope, nativeRef: NativeRef) => ObservedNode["freshness"] | "disconnected" | undefined }): readonly EvidenceLoader[]. Read EvidenceLoader/EvidenceContent/EvidenceRequest from the landed src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts (wb-g1g.1) and the reader signatures from the landed reader modules at claim time; never re-declare or re-implement either.
- Layer 1: a loader is constructed only when input.grants() (read once at construction) contains the row's requiredGrant as an exact string AND the matching reader is supplied; malformed or unknown grant entries are ignored (deny). Layer 2: every load(request) re-reads input.grants() and throws CapabilityError("authorization", ...) before touching the reader when the exact grant is absent.
- Routing: loader.provider equals the row provider; canLoad(ref) is the row's shape check only (uuid shape for claude-message, validated operation id for forge-operation, the furnace reader's own Attempt-id predicate); load(request) throws CapabilityError("validation") when request.nativeRef.provider !== loader.provider or !canLoad(request.evidenceRef) -- the store routes provider-first, the loader never guesses.
- Assembly: load returns the full EvidenceContent (docs/20 ruling 1): kind, provider, capturedAt, bytes, truncated, preview (the reader's lines passed through the idempotent shared sanitizers redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText from src/workbench/redaction.ts; no new lines, no raw payload retained), sourceBasis only when digest-shaped (sha256:<64 hex> or the identity digest shape), otherwise omitted; freshness "stale" when owningFreshness reports stale, unknown, disconnected or undefined, "current" only for "current"; producerReceipt passed through when the reader supplies one. Reader failures propagate as CapabilityError with the reader's category (transport/authorization/unavailable/validation), never converted into a loaded entry; each loader exposes freshnessOf(request) so the store can label a transport failure against a disconnected source as transport plus stale.
- Anything else (hyperunix, reactivefiber, beads, unknown providers): no loader is produced, so the store yields unavailable: no-loader; the factory never fabricates a loader or a preview.
- Frozen outputs; no Date.now (capturedAt comes from the reader); no SDK imports; node:* imports only if the landed readers require them.

Out of scope: src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts (wb-g1g.1 owns it), the three reader modules (wb-6ze.8/.10/.11 own them), EvidenceStore construction and the load-evidence/abortAll dialog wiring (owner's wiring slice in src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts -- HOT), src/index.ts (HOT), hosts, grant settings parsing, any live SDK tier.

acceptance_criteria:
All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, base 0ef5aeb or later per BOUNDARY.md).
1. docs/workbench/20-evidence-loader-contract.md § "Types": "Grant gating is two-layered and exact-string: loaders are constructed only when the host grant set contains `requiredGrant`, and every `load` re-reads the live grant set so mid-view revocation refuses with `unauthorized`." -> with grants() returning ["claude:transcript"] and all three readers supplied, createEvidenceLoaders returns exactly one loader whose provider is "claude-agent-sdk"; with [] it returns an empty array; with all three grants it returns three loaders in row order. A loader constructed under a grant whose grants() later returns without it rejects load with CapabilityError category "authorization" and the reader spy records zero calls; "claude:transcript " (trailing space), "CLAUDE:TRANSCRIPT" and "claude:*" never satisfy the check (docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Authorization design": "Treat unknown permission data as deny.").
2. docs/workbench/20 § "Types": "`nativeRef` is required because evidence ref strings are not globally namespaced; producer routing keys off `nativeRef.provider` first, with `canLoad(evidenceRef)` as a shape check inside that producer only." and § "Owner rulings on the design conflicts" 3: "Loaders take the full request, not a bare ref; routing is provider-first." -> each loader's canLoad accepts exactly its row's ref shape and rejects the other two rows' shapes; load with request.nativeRef.provider "forge" on the claude loader rejects with category "validation" and calls no reader; the test enumerates all nine provider x ref-shape pairs and exactly three delegate to a reader.
3. docs/workbench/20 § "Producer mapping": rows "claude-agent-sdk session | `claude-message:<uuid>` | ... | `claude:transcript`", "furnace run | native Attempt id listed on the owning run node | ... | `furnace:inspect`", "forge operation | `forge-operation:<operation_id>` | ... | `forge:inspect`", "anything else | — | `unavailable: no-loader`, a visible unknown | —" -> EVIDENCE_LOADER_ROWS deep-equals exactly those three rows (a mutation test appending a fourth "hyperunix" row fails the pinned-table assertion); no loader is ever produced for a provider outside the table even when a grant such as "hyperunix:inspect" is present.
4. docs/workbench/20 § "Owner rulings" 1: "`loaded` equals the full `EvidenceContent` (kind, sourceBasis, freshness included)." and § "Types": "`sourceBasis` accepts digest-shaped values only." -> a reader result carrying sourceBasis "sha256:" + 64 hex is passed through; "main", "/tmp/x" and "sha256:abc" are omitted (never defaulted, never truncated into a fake digest); bytes, truncated, capturedAt and producerReceipt are copied from the reader, not recomputed; preview lines equal the reader's lines after the idempotent sanitizers and the factory adds no line (docs/20 ruling 2: "The double redaction in the sanitizer order is deliberate and idempotent." -- a reader line containing "\x1b[31m", U+202E or U+200B comes out stripped; an already-sanitized line comes out byte-identical).
5. docs/workbench/20 § "Refusal and freshness rules": "Stale or disconnected owning nodes label loaded evidence stale; a failed read against a disconnected source is transport plus stale. A loaded entry never upgrades projection freshness and never changes node status text or tone. Transport success never implies verification." -> owningFreshness "stale", "unknown", "disconnected" or undefined yields freshness "stale"; only "current" yields "current"; a reader CapabilityError("transport") propagates with the same category and loader.freshnessOf(request) reports "stale" for the disconnected owner; a forge reader result whose domain verdict is failed or partial is returned as its own kind/status, and the string "verified" appears nowhere in the module source nor in any emitted content under the fixture.
6. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" (Details): "Large content loaded only on focus." -> createEvidenceLoaders calls no reader (spy count 0 after construction); only load() delegates, exactly once per call.
7. Negative controls: a request whose scope differs from the owning node's scope is rejected "authorization" without a reader call; the module never imports an SDK or node:child_process (static assertion on import specifiers); a request for a provider with no row (e.g. "hyperunix") finds no loader in the returned array (the store renders no-loader) and the factory exposes no fallback path.

title: W16-F/VC-4: pure bounded workflow_control reply builder over the landed decision core (requested/acknowledged/result kept distinct with native echo, typed sanitized refusal replies for denied decisions, destructive-confirmation state carried never minted, byte-capped compact JSON through shared sanitizers, transport success never domain verification); Pi tool registration and provider adapters excluded
description:
Gap: docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "First public Pi tools (proposed)" specifies "workflow_control(ref,action,params?): explicit native action after permission/preconditions; returns requested/acknowledged/result distinct." The decision module landed as wb-69g.1 (src/workbench/control.ts, closed) and the Furnace adapter is wb-69g.3 (open), but no bounded sanitized REPLY surface exists to shape a control decision plus adapter phase receipts into the compact structured tool reply the spec requires. workflow_catalog/inspect (wb-69g.2), workflow_observe (wb-752.2) and workflow_execute (wb-69g.5) all have reply builders; control does not.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free; red-first):
- src/workbench/control-reply.ts (new): buildControlReply over inputs {decision from the landed control.ts core, phase receipts requested/acknowledged/result, native echo, byte budget}. Pure: never invokes adapters or SDK clients, never registers a Pi tool.
- test/workbench-control-reply.test.ts (new): red first.

Behavior:
- Denied decision (missing per-verb grant control:<provider>.<action>, observer-only scope, unconfirmed ownership, guessed action) renders a typed sanitized refusal reply; no phase receipt is fabricated.
- requested/acknowledged/result stay distinct fields, never collapsed; result-absent renders acknowledged-only and never reads as completion.
- Native echo is carried observed-not-verified; transport success is never labeled domain verification.
- Destructive-action confirmation state comes from the decision core and is carried, never bypassed or minted by the builder.
- Reply is byte-capped compact JSON with an honest truncated flag; every string routes through the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (standing invariant), including adversarial ANSI/control characters in echo text.

Excluded: Pi tool registration (src/index.ts is hot and held until release), provider adapters (wb-69g.3; blocked Claude interrupt gap wb-69g.4 stays untouched), src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts (hot), src/workflow/* (hot).
Files: src/workbench/control-reply.ts (new), test/workbench-control-reply.test.ts (new). Specs: docs/workbench/11 (First public Pi tools), docs/workbench/15 W16, docs/workbench/06 (grants), docs/workbench/02.

Missing edges do not imply independence." The graph view (:328-343) already renders at most two relations per node with a direction glyph and `[provenance.source]`; the details view does not. wb-g1g.2 (open) delivers the PURE selector selectLinkedTopology(relationsInput, focusKey, caps) in src/workbench/topology-slice.ts and explicitly excludes "src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts and any details-view rendering"; wb-g1g.1 (open) edits the same details branch for evidence rendering. Scope (atomic, pure layout, hot-file free): in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts ONLY the details branch of layoutInspector. When InspectorModel carries the wb-g1g.2 selector output for the selected node (an optional model.topology?: (node) => LinkedTopologySlice read side, mirroring wb-g1g.1's optional model.evidence pattern), render after the Evidence rows: `Upstream (n)` then one row per edge `<dir> <relation class> [<provenance.source>[ @<observedAt>]] <neighbour provider/type/id>`, then `Downstream (n)` likewise, with relation class labels exactly the docs/09 set (declared dependency / observed causal / lifecycle ownership (native-confirmed) / grouping / inferred hypothesis); cycle entries and unknown dynamic edges render as `reference -> <ref>` rows, never as tree children; fan-out beyond the slice caps renders one `… +k more (bounded)` row; a slice labelled incomplete-trace renders `Topology: incomplete trace`; an empty slice renders `Topology: no observed relations (missing edges do not imply independence)`. Every string passes the file's safe() (safeWorkflowTerminalText) path, the inspector's shared sanitizer route, never raw provenance text. When model.topology is absent the details view renders byte-identical to today (the current `Relations:` line stays as-is in that case). No new InspectorAction, no new keys, no new state fields; reduceInspectorKey unchanged. Gap (measured at rig HEAD, branch workbench/implementation-program, base 23404b4+): docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "First public Pi tools (proposed)" lists seven tools; W16 siblings cover catalog/inspect (wb-69g.2), observe (wb-752.2), control decision core (wb-69g.1, landed in src/workbench/control.ts) and the Furnace control adapter (wb-69g.3). workflow_execute has NO bead and NO source: grep finds no workflow_execute anywhere in src/; the registered workbench tools in src/index.ts registerWorkbenchTools (guard at :2480) are workbench_catalog, workflow_validate, workflow_catalog and workflow_compare only.

Scope (atomic, pure module): src/workbench/execute.ts (new) mirroring the landed wb-69g.1 decision-core pattern in src/workbench/control.ts: decideExecute(request, grants) admission decision plus buildWorkflowExecuteReply over an INJECTED launch outcome. Typed refusals (missing execute-authority grant, non-digest definitionRef, unknown hostMode, malformed policy). The module never launches anything itself and never imports an SDK; actual host invocation wiring and Pi tool registration are excluded (a later registration bead adds the tool name to the pinned WORKBENCH_TOOLS census literal per the wb-cax.4 note). Files: src/workbench/execute.ts (new), test/workbench-execute.test.ts (new).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-execute.test.ts fails before src/workbench/execute.ts exists. Base 23404b4 or later. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

E1. Tool shape. docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md section "First public Pi tools (proposed)": "workflow_execute(definitionRef,input,hostMode,policy?): authorized launch; returns logical invocation and native references, not false completion." -> decideExecute accepts exactly {definitionRef, input, hostMode, policy?}; the reply built from an injected launch outcome carries the logical invocation reference and the native references the launch reported, and a status that is launch-level only (e.g. accepted/launched/refused); asserting a completed/successful terminal state from a launch outcome is impossible by construction (falsifier test).
E2. Immutable digest. docs/workbench/11 section "Operator actions versus designer edits": "Design-time edits occur against versioned source; execution against immutable digest." -> a definitionRef that is not digest-pinned is refused with a typed diagnostic before any grant check consumes it.
E3. Exact execute authority. docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md: "Registered descriptors do not grant access." and "Catalog discovery independently requires exact `discover:<capabilityId>`." plus docs/workbench/02 WB-034: "list/inspect never grant invoke." -> admission requires one exact execute-authority grant distinct from workbench:design, workbench:observe and every discover:/inspect: grant; proven both ways (grant present admits, grant absent refuses typed); a grant set holding only discover:/inspect:/design/observe grants NEVER admits (falsifier).
E4. No node-permission leakage. docs/workbench/06: "Invocation requires every explicit producer permission in the descriptor." -> the reply never claims or implies node-level capability permissions; it echoes the policy input verbatim-bounded and leaves per-node admission to the host registry seam.
E5. hostMode allowlist. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Install profile" separates "embedded Pi extension with local Claude SDK host" from "optional headless executor library/process for detached runs" -> hostMode is a closed allowlist (embedded, detached); an unknown hostMode is a typed refusal, never a guessed default.
E6. Sanitized bounded reply. Every string in the reply routes through the shared sanitizers (src/workbench/redaction.ts) and the reply is byte-capped with a visible truncation marker; raw launch payloads are never retained.
E7. Purity. The module performs no I/O, imports no SDK and never invokes the registry; vitest covers refusal and admission paths; biome clean; no any; no inline imports; no existing test weakened.

title: W21-B: observation recovery and bounded-query size benchmark receipt (ingest events/s, retained memory, disconnect -> stale -> reconnect-alone falsifier -> per-snapshot reconcile latency, evicted-cursor partial-gap detection, query/window/relations/events byte sizes) at 1k/100k default limits and 10k/100k bench-only limits; measurement-only, src untouched
description:
Gap (measured at rig 1fc74f0): docs/workbench/14 § "Performance benchmark" lists metrics no bench records: "observer ingest events/s and projection memory", "recover snapshot/cursor latency" and "Pi model tool response size under bounded queries". qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs (receipts cmd_9572ac580306, cmd_4ff4ffabcbe0) measures navigation only; wb-9x5.1 (W21, ready) measures grouped navigation/layout/terminal bytes; test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts:11 asserts one query's examined count (<4) and bytes (<2000) with no receipt and no recovery; test/workbench-observation.test.ts:43 proves "reconnect alone cannot restore current without snapshot" at toy scale only. The recovery API exists in src/workbench/observation.ts: disconnect():356, reconnect():369, refresh():318, markStale():344, events():540 (completeness "complete" | "partial-gap"), query():477, window():448, relations():397, stats():558, MAX_DEFAULT:93 {maxEvents 20000, maxNodes 2000, maxEdges 4000, maxPayloadBytes 4096, maxQuery 100}. furnace_observe (src/index.ts:2555-2563) polls once (maxPolls 1) and relies on projection.refresh/markStale for freshness, so recovery cost at scale is an unmeasured VC-4/VC-5 claim.

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, hot-file free; no production limit or behavior change):
• qa/workbench/observation-recovery-receipt.mjs (new, pure, no src/ or dist/ import): buildFixture({seed, nodes, events, providers}) -> plain data {snapshots: NativeSnapshot[], updates: ObservationEvent[], shape} (deterministic: no Date.now or Math.random in the measured path, timestamps derived from one fixed epoch, same rules as the header of test/helpers/perf-fixtures.ts; provider mix forge/furnace/claude-agent-sdk; one invocationId and one scope); measureRecovery(ProjectionClass, fixture, {limits?, provider, queryLimit}) -> measurement (exported so vitest passes the src class and the CLI passes the dist class); assessRecovery(measurement) -> {findings: {rule, detail}[], realised: boolean}; buildReceipt(input) -> frozen plain object {contract: "workbench.observation-recovery/v1", utc, revision, node, arch, platform, cpus, passes, findings, realised, pass}.
• measureRecovery, per pass: ingest every update (ingestMs, eventsPerSecond, applied/duplicate/out-of-order counts); retained = stats(); heapGrowthBytes labelled "transient-inclusive"; disconnect(provider) -> staleAfterDisconnect (nodes whose freshness !== "current", counted through bounded query pages) and disconnectMs; reconnect(provider) ALONE -> currentRegainedWithoutSnapshot (must be 0; otherwise finding "reconnect-restored-current"); refresh(snapshot) once per node of that provider -> per-call latency p50/p95/max over single refresh() calls and reconcileMs until that provider's stale count returns to 0 (otherwise finding "stale-after-full-refresh"); events({scope, limit: queryLimit, after: <a cursor older than the retained window>}) -> completeness must be "partial-gap" with gapDetectMs (otherwise finding "gap-not-detected"); events({after: <a retained cursor>}) -> "complete" with resumeMs; bounded query sizes: maxBytes of JSON.stringify for query({scope, invocationId, limit: queryLimit}), window({scope, invocationId, offset: 0, limit: queryLimit}), relations({scope, from: <key>, limit: queryLimit}) and events({scope, limit: queryLimit}) plus rowsReturned per method (rows > limit is finding "limit-exceeded"; any "\x1b" in a serialized result is finding "ansi-in-result").
• Two passes in ONE receipt: pass "default-limits" = new ProjectionClass() with no limits argument (caps never raised), 1,000 nodes / 100,000 events; pass "bench-only-limits" = new ProjectionClass({maxNodes: 12000, maxEdges: 24000, maxEvents: 20000, maxQuery: 100}), 10,000 nodes / 100,000 events, limits recorded in the receipt and never entering src/.
• qa/workbench/observation-recovery-bench.mjs (new CLI; imports ONLY ../../dist/workbench/observation.js, ./observation-recovery-receipt.mjs, node:os and node:fs): builds both fixtures, runs both passes, prints the receipt as one JSON line and writes it to $W21_RECOVERY_RECEIPT when set BEFORE exiting; exit 2 when a realised fixture shape is below 1,000/100,000 (pass A) or 10,000/100,000 (pass B) — the measurement would not be the claimed shape; exit 1 when findings is non-empty (a measured semantic violation, recorded honestly, never tuned away); exit 0 otherwise. No recovery-latency threshold exists in the specs, so latency is reported, never judged.
• test/workbench-observation-recovery-receipt.test.ts (new, offline): imports the receipt module; runs measureRecovery with the src ObservationProjection class (import from ../src/workbench/observation.js) on a 200-node / 2,000-event fixture and asserts every measurement field is a finite number, currentRegainedWithoutSnapshot === 0, staleAfterDisconnect equals the provider's node count, stale count 0 after the full refresh, partial-gap detected for an evicted cursor and complete for a retained one; asserts assessRecovery raises each finding for synthetic violating measurements; asserts fixture determinism (same seed -> identical JSON, different seed -> different); reads qa/workbench/observation-recovery-bench.mjs as text and asserts its import specifiers are exactly the allowed set and that the only "maxNodes" literal is inside the bench-only pass object (pass A constructs with no argument).
• forge.toml: one additive [build.commands.observation-recovery-bench] block (command "node qa/workbench/observation-recovery-bench.mjs", timeout 300), NOT added to the default [build] gate list (same placement as inspector-bench).

Out of scope: any src/ edit (observation.ts belongs to wb-6ze.2 this run), qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs, test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts, wb-9x5.1's grouped fixture (a later bead may re-run this bench over it), docs/TRACEABILITY.md and docs/workbench/10 (acceptance owner reconciles the measured receipt), cap changes.
Files: qa/workbench/observation-recovery-receipt.mjs (new), qa/workbench/observation-recovery-bench.mjs (new), test/workbench-observation-recovery-receipt.test.ts (new), forge.toml (one additive block). Specs: docs/workbench/14 (Performance benchmark; Truth labels and release gates), 09 (Experimental projection implementation; Acceptance/negative controls 3 and 9; Freshness and ambiguity), 10 (Rendering pipeline), 15 W21, 02 WB-036.

title: W14/VC-5-C: pure attention and bottleneck selector over ObservationProjection (waiting/stale/unknown/disconnected counts, top measured open intervals from source intervals, dependency-chain critical path only as partial-estimated else incomplete-trace with reasons; caller clock, bounded, sanitized); inspector and tool wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig 1fc74f0): docs/workbench/10 § "Four views" (Overview) requires "status and counts, compact nested tree, active operations, attention panel and top measured bottlenecks" with the critical path "shown as *partial/estimated* when relationships/times incomplete", and docs/workbench/09 § "Aggregates and profiling" requires measured-vs-estimated separation with "incomplete trace" whenever intervals or dependencies are missing. Today src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts:156-157 prints two CONSTANT strings regardless of data ('Attention: stale/unknown is last-known state, not live progress.' and 'Critical path: incomplete trace (no complete dependency/interval proof).'), pinned by test/workbench-inspector.test.ts:112-116 and :195-198. Nothing in src/ computes attention items, bottlenecks or a dependency-chain estimate from observed data: grep -rn 'bottleneck\|criticalPath' src returns only designer.ts:183/236 (criticalPath "unestablished" for run comparisons; hot, untouched) and the inspector constants. wb-6ze.2 (ancestor aggregates in observation.ts) pins criticalPath 'unestablished' and lists "concurrency/critical-path profiling" out of scope; wb-6ze.1 owns the inspector file this run; wb-752.2 builds the workflow_observe reply. This bead supplies the pure selector both consumers wire later.

Scope (atomic, additive, new file, hot-file free): src/workbench/attention.ts exporting
• ATTENTION_CONTRACT = "workbench.attention/v1".
• selectAttention(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "relations">, input: { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; now: string; limit?: number; bottlenecks?: number }): AttentionReport.
• AttentionReport = { contract: typeof ATTENTION_CONTRACT; basis: "observed"; now: string; examined: { nodes: number; truncated: boolean }; counts: { active; waiting; success; failure; unknown; stale; disconnected; withInterval; withoutInterval }; disconnectedProviders: string[]; bottlenecks: { key; nativeRef; title; tone; freshness; openMs: number; measured: true }[]; unmeasured: number; clockSkew: number; criticalPath: { label: "incomplete-trace"; reasons: ("no-dependency-edges" | "missing-intervals" | "open-intervals" | "hypothesis-edges" | "cycle" | "truncated")[] } | { label: "partial-estimated"; keys: string[]; measuredMs: number; coverage: { chainNodes: number; dependencyEdges: number }; caveat: string }; clockCaveat: string }.
• Rules. `now` is the CALLER's clock (ISO-8601 with timezone; the module never calls Date.now()). Nodes come from ONE bounded projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit: input.limit ?? 100}) call; examined.truncated propagates its truncated flag. openMs = now − interval.startedAt for nodes with statusTone 'active' or 'waiting' that have interval.startedAt and no endedAt; a producer startedAt later than now clamps openMs to 0 and increments clockSkew; nodes without an interval are counted in unmeasured and never ranked; ranking is openMs descending then key ascending (deterministic); bottlenecks.length <= input.bottlenecks ?? 5 and every entry carries measured: true. counts.stale = nodes with freshness !== 'current'; counts.disconnected = nodes with sourceConnectionState 'disconnected'; disconnectedProviders = sorted distinct nativeRef.provider of those nodes. Tones are counted separately (waiting is never folded into active or stale).
• criticalPath. Dependency edges come from projection.relations({scope, from: key, limit}) for examined keys only, kind 'dependency' only. 'partial-estimated' requires ALL of: at least one dependency edge among examined nodes; no 'hypothesis' edge among examined nodes; no cycle on dependency edges; query not truncated; every node on the chosen chain has a COMPLETE interval (startedAt and endedAt). measuredMs is the sum of complete interval durations along the longest-duration dependency chain (DAG longest path); keys lists that chain in dependency order; the caveat literal is "Observed dependency edges and complete source intervals only; missing edges do not imply independence." Anything else returns incomplete-trace carrying EVERY applicable reason. The label is never "exact" or "complete" and no number is emitted without the partial-estimated label.
• clockCaveat literal: "openMs uses the caller clock against producer startedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled."
• Every title passes redactWorkbenchText (import from src/workbench/redaction.ts; do not edit) and is cut to 120 characters; control characters never survive; JSON.stringify(report).length < 16384 at limit 100 / bottlenecks 5.

Out of scope: rendering in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (wb-6ze.1 / wb-g1g.1 territory this run), the workflow_observe reply (wb-752.2) and src/index.ts, any edit to src/workbench/observation.ts (wb-6ze.2 owns the aggregate API; this bead only CALLS query/relations), token/cost/retry metrics (no producer supplies them), designer.ts (hot).
Files: src/workbench/attention.ts (new), test/workbench-attention.test.ts (new). Specs: docs/workbench/10 (Four views; Rendering pipeline; Failure and deception defenses; Timeline), 09 (Aggregates and profiling; Relationships are typed and provenanced; Freshness and ambiguity; Data retention and privacy), 14 (Truth labels and release gates), 02 WB-029.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-attention.test.ts fails before src/workbench/attention.ts exists. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, 1fc74f0+).

B1. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Overview: "header (name, identity, native owner, freshness), status and counts, compact nested tree, active operations, attention panel and top measured bottlenecks. Critical path must be shown as *partial/estimated* when relationships/times incomplete." -> fixture of 12 observed nodes at caller clock T (4 active with startedAt, 2 waiting with startedAt, 1 active without any interval, 3 success, 1 failure, 1 unknown): bottlenecks lists the 5 largest openMs in descending order with exact values T − startedAt and measured: true on each; the active node without an interval is counted in unmeasured (=== 1) and absent from bottlenecks; counts.{active,waiting,success,failure,unknown,withInterval,withoutInterval} equal the fixture exactly.
B2. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics. If dependencies or interval bounds are missing, suppress precise critical path claims and show \"incomplete trace\". Derive latency decomposition only with valid source intervals." -> (a) no dependency edges -> incomplete-trace with reason "no-dependency-edges"; (b) a dependency chain where one node lacks endedAt -> "open-intervals"; (c) one chain node without any interval -> "missing-intervals"; (d) a hypothesis edge among examined nodes -> "hypothesis-edges" even when every interval is complete; (e) a truncated query -> "truncated"; in each of (a)-(e) JSON.stringify(report.criticalPath) contains neither "measuredMs" nor any digit-only duration.
B3. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "Missing edges do not imply independence." and docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Graph: "Cycles/unknown dynamic edges represented explicitly as \"references\" rather than rendered as a fake acyclic plan." -> a complete-interval dependency chain A->B->C (durations 10 s, 20 s, 30 s) plus an unrelated complete node D yields {label:"partial-estimated", keys:[A,B,C], measuredMs: 60000, coverage:{chainNodes:3, dependencyEdges:2}} with the exact caveat literal "Observed dependency edges and complete source intervals only; missing edges do not imply independence."; adding dependency C->A yields incomplete-trace with reason "cycle"; the string "exact" never appears in any report.
B4. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Failure and deception defenses": "STALLED vs WAITING vs STALE vs UNKNOWN must not be confused. Spinner should not imply work progressed." and docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Freshness and ambiguity": "UI shows STALE/UNKNOWN visibly." -> after projection.disconnect("furnace") counts.stale and counts.disconnected rise by exactly the furnace node count and disconnectedProviders deep-equals ["furnace"]; a stale active node still ranks by its measured openMs and carries freshness "stale"; counts.waiting is unchanged by the disconnect and counts.unknown counts only statusTone "unknown".
B5. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Timeline": "Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps." -> a node whose startedAt is later than now yields openMs 0 and clockSkew 1; report.clockCaveat equals "openMs uses the caller clock against producer startedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled."; vi.spyOn(Date, "now") records zero calls during selectAttention; the module source read as text contains no "Date.now".
B6. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Data retention and privacy": "Tenant/workspace boundaries apply at correlation queries, not just at individual SDK calls." and docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "Pi observation tools paginate/filter/limit and return compact JSON, never rendered ANSI." -> nodes ingested under a second workspace/principal never appear in the report; with 1,000 fixture nodes and limit 100, examined.nodes === 100, examined.truncated === true and JSON.stringify(report).length < 16384; a title containing "Bearer abc123" and "\x1b[31m" appears in bottlenecks[].title with "[REDACTED]" and without any control character.
B7. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." -> brute-force falsifier: a seeded deterministic fixture (fixed seed, no Math.random or Date.now in the measured path, same rules as the header of test/helpers/perf-fixtures.ts) of 200 nodes with dependency, grouping and hypothesis edges and mixed complete/open/missing intervals: selectAttention's counts, bottlenecks and criticalPath deep-equal an independent brute-force computation written in the test.
B8. Gate: ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on both new files; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-attention.test.ts test/workbench-observation.test.ts test/workbench-inspector.test.ts green; src/workbench/observation.ts, src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts, src/workbench/designer.ts and src/index.ts byte-identical to the base (git diff --stat vs 1fc74f0 lists only the two new files); do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md (acceptance owner reconciles).
notes: Sr. Engineer constraint 2026-10-15: selector derives ONLY from observed counts and provably measured open intervals; partial/incomplete traces yield an explicit unknown critical path, never a fabricated bottleneck; pure module; author strings sanitized. Base 1fc74f0+.

title: VC-7/W18-B: pure native executable identity observation (realpath + sha256 for absolute paths, PATH-resolved binaries labelled mutable-path, SDK default executable labelled unsupported, never executes) plus reattach comparison that never upgrades unknown to same; detached host wiring excluded
description:
Gap: docs/workbench/15 names "native immutable deployment refs" as VC-7 acceptance and docs/workbench/08 says native executable identity is an unestablished release obligation; W18 (wb-5w0) notes "Native binaries ... not claimed" and W22 (wb-cax) notes "Full release/install native binary identity ... remain open". At rig ad3cf6e the detached host hard-codes `nativeRuntimeIdentity: "unsupported"` (src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:82 and :96) and its runtimeClosure comment reads "Native executables launched by SDK defaults/PATH still have unsupported identity."; src/workbench/providers/forge.ts:80 launches ServerConnection.spawn("forge"), a bare PATH-resolved name; the Claude Agent SDK's Options.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1984) "Uses the built-in executable if not specified." Nothing in src/ can observe, pin or compare the bytes of a native executable, so no host can honestly report which binary it launched or refuse reattachment when that binary changed.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/executable-identity.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-executable-identity.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const EXECUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT = 'workbench.executable-identity/v1'
- export type ExecutableIdentityReason = 'sdk-default-executable' | 'not-found' | 'not-a-file' | 'not-executable' | 'symlink-depth' | 'too-large' | 'unreadable' | 'path-resolved' | 'shadowed-candidates' | 'search-truncated' (frozen set; nothing else is ever emitted).
- export interface ExecutableObservation { contractVersion: typeof EXECUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT; requested: string | undefined; resolution: 'absolute' | 'path-search' | 'unresolved'; resolvedPath?: string; realPath?: string; symlinkHops: number; digest?: string (sha256:<hex>); sizeBytes?: number; mode?: number; candidates: number; immutability: 'digest-observed' | 'mutable-path' | 'unsupported'; reasons: readonly ExecutableIdentityReason[]; observedAt: string }
- export function observeExecutableIdentity(input: { command: string | undefined; cwd: string; path: string | undefined; observedAt: string; maxBytes?: number; maxSearchEntries?: number; maxSymlinkHops?: number }): ExecutableObservation — synchronous; reads only through node:fs (lstat, readlink, stat, chunked reads for hashing — never readFileSync of a whole binary); never imports node:child_process; never reads process.env (PATH is an explicit input); never throws for a missing, unreadable, non-regular, non-executable or oversized target — those are 'unresolved'/'unsupported' with a reason.
  • command undefined or empty -> resolution 'unresolved', immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['sdk-default-executable'] (the honest answer for the Claude built-in executable and any SDK default).
  • command containing a path separator -> resolved against cwd; symlinks followed hop by hop (count hops; above maxSymlinkHops, default 16, -> 'unsupported' with 'symlink-depth'); must be a regular file with an execute bit; hashed with sha256 when sizeBytes <= maxBytes (default 512 MiB) -> resolution 'absolute', immutability 'digest-observed'; oversize -> digest omitted, immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['too-large'].
  • bare command -> PATH searched in order (split on path.delimiter; at most maxSearchEntries, default 64, further entries ignored and 'search-truncated' recorded; relative or empty entries resolved against cwd); the first regular executable file wins; candidates counts every searched entry holding a same-named executable; resolution 'path-search'; the digest IS observed but immutability is 'mutable-path' with reasons ['path-resolved'] plus 'shadowed-candidates' when candidates > 1. A digest never upgrades a PATH-resolved binary to 'digest-observed'.
  • Result and its reasons are frozen; resolvedPath and realPath pass through redactWorkbenchText (paths may embed tokens); absent fields mean not observed, never a default.
- export function compareExecutableIdentity(recorded: ExecutableObservation, current: ExecutableObservation): { verdict: 'same' | 'changed' | 'unknown'; differences: readonly string[] } — 'same' only when both digests are present and equal AND both immutability values are 'digest-observed'; 'changed' when both digests are present and differ; otherwise 'unknown' (a mutable-path or unsupported side can never yield 'same'); differences names each differing field (digest, realPath, sizeBytes, mode, immutability, resolution).

Out of scope: editing src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts (in flight under wb-6hb.1; the 'unsupported' literal is W18's later wiring point), src/workbench/providers/forge.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts, src/workbench/identity.ts; discovering the Claude built-in executable path from SDK internals; remote host authentication; Furnace ExecutorApp. If acceptance cannot be met without touching a hot or reserved file, stop and return blocked.

Files: src/workbench/executable-identity.ts (new); test/workbench-executable-identity.test.ts (new; mkdtemp fixtures with explicit modes only; nothing is executed). Imports: node:fs, node:path, node:crypto; redactWorkbenchText from src/workbench/redaction.ts (hot, import only). Specs: docs/workbench/08 (Separate four identities; Experimental immutable receipt; Optional local detached profile; Run recovery and journal design), docs/workbench/17 (Versioning / distribution), docs/workbench/12 (Supply chain; Credential boundaries), docs/workbench/15 (Vertical cuts VC-7), docs/workbench/02 WB-014/WB-041.
acceptance_criteria:
All criteria quote docs/workbench specs in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, HEAD ad3cf6e). Red-first: test/workbench-executable-identity.test.ts fails before src/workbench/executable-identity.ts exists. All fixtures live under a mkdtemp directory with explicit modes; nothing is executed.

B1. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Separate four identities": "2. Deployment: immutable digest of artifact, dependencies, configuration and compatible host ABI." -> for a fixture file written with mode 0o755 and referenced by absolute path, observeExecutableIdentity returns resolution 'absolute', immutability 'digest-observed', digest equal to 'sha256:' plus the hex sha256 of the same bytes, sizeBytes equal to the byte length, symlinkHops 0, candidates 1 and reasons []; observing process.execPath by absolute path also yields 'digest-observed', and two observations of it are deep-equal apart from observedAt.

B2. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Experimental immutable receipt": "A model alias, mutable PATH or SDK default executable must not be advertised as an immutable native deployment merely because the JavaScript client is pinned." -> the bare name 'forge' (the literal src/workbench/providers/forge.ts:80 spawns) with a PATH of two temp directories each holding an executable 'forge' resolves to the FIRST directory with resolution 'path-search', candidates 2, immutability 'mutable-path' and reasons containing 'path-resolved' and 'shadowed-candidates' although digest is present; reversing the PATH order changes realPath and digest; command undefined yields resolution 'unresolved', immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['sdk-default-executable'] and no digest.

B3. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Experimental immutable receipt": "The identity audit also pins explicitly resolved loaded SDK JavaScript files, rather than assuming a lockfile/archive proves the installed bytes." -> a symlink chain link2 -> link1 -> binary yields realPath equal to the binary's realpath, symlinkHops 2 and the same digest as the direct observation; a chain longer than maxSymlinkHops yields immutability 'unsupported' with reasons ['symlink-depth'] and no digest; a mode 0o644 file as the only PATH candidate yields resolution 'unresolved' with reasons ['not-executable']; a directory named like the command yields 'not-a-file'; a missing command yields 'not-found'; none of these throws.

B4. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Run recovery and journal design": "Do not silently migrate a running invocation to new source/registry version." and docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Versioning / distribution": "Pin immutable deploy artifact for reproducible observations." -> compareExecutableIdentity returns verdict 'same' for two digest-observed observations of identical bytes even when observedAt differs; 'changed' with differences including 'digest' after one byte of the fixture is rewritten; and 'unknown' whenever either side lacks a digest or is 'mutable-path' or 'unsupported' — a mutable-path pair with equal digests is 'unknown', never 'same'.

B5. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md section "Optional local detached profile": "Furnace-hosted durability and native executable identity are separate, unestablished release obligations." and docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Vertical cuts" VC-7: "Remote host authentication, reattachment, native immutable deployment refs, crash/uncertain-operation conformance." -> the module's own source, read by the test, contains none of 'node:child_process', 'process.env' or 'Date.now'; a 64-byte fixture observed with maxBytes 16 yields 'unsupported' with reasons ['too-large'] and no digest; the observation, its reasons array and the comparison result are frozen and JSON round-trip stable.

B6. docs/workbench/12-security.md section "Supply chain": "Pin SDK versions, package/artifact digests and provenance." and section "Credential boundaries": "redact tokens from logs, UI, recordings and failure messages." -> a PATH entry whose directory name contains 'Bearer abc123' never appears raw in resolvedPath, realPath or reasons (the redactWorkbenchText marker replaces it); a PATH with 100 entries and the match only in entry 90 is searched for at most maxSearchEntries (64) and reports resolution 'unresolved' with reasons containing 'search-truncated' rather than a certain 'not-found'.

B7. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-014: "Workflow invocation carries definition, immutable implementation basis and logical invocation ID; native refs remain intact." and WB-041: "Optional detached workbench host permits Pi client disconnect/reconnect, without falsely claiming crash durability." -> contractVersion is exactly 'workbench.executable-identity/v1' on every observation; the whole suite runs with no TTY, no spawned process and no network; test/workbench-local-detached.test.ts stays green and git diff --name-only shows only the two new files.

Process: red-first; ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on both files; no any; no inline imports; never weaken or delete existing tests; forge run lint / typing / test green in the worktree; hot and reserved files untouched; do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md.

title: VC-7/W18-A: detached-host fault-injection conformance tier (effect-then-crash before host result, SIGTERM on a running owned host, cancel isolation across two hosts, shutdown unresolvedEffects) with exactly-once effect markers and an evidence-grade receipt; measurement-only, dist imports, src untouched

title: W22-C: offline vendored native-SDK pin falsifier (vendor/README.md SHA-256 table == tarball bytes; package-lock file:vendor entries carry inBundle+integrity+matching version; bundledDependencies covers every file:vendor dependency; no orphan tarball)
description:
Gap: vendor/README.md publishes SHA-256 values for forge-sdk-0.1.0.tgz, furnace-sdk-0.1.0.tgz and hyperunix-sdk-0.1.0.tgz as a prose table. src/workbench/identity.ts verifies package-lock integrity against vendor bytes at invocation-identity capture time (test "pins actual package.json, package-lock.json and local vendor artifact bytes"), but nothing in the portable gate checks that (a) the README table equals the on-disk SHA-256 of each tarball, (b) every `file:vendor/*.tgz` dependency in package.json is listed in `bundledDependencies` and has a package-lock `packages["node_modules/<name>"]` entry with `resolved: "file:vendor/<file>"`, `inBundle: true`, a version matching the tarball filename and a well-formed integrity, or (c) no tarball exists without a README row and a package.json dependency (orphan). docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md § "Clean external install" records the real regression this guards: cmd_8d6d9f378d88 failed because "npm could not resolve local native SDK tarballs before extracting the parent package" until the SDKs were bundled; today that would only be caught by the network-requiring install-smoke tier.

Deliver: test/workbench-vendor-pins.test.ts (new vitest; node:crypto sha256 over vendor/*.tgz; parses the README markdown table rows `| <file> | <sha256> |`, package.json and package-lock.json; no network, no npm child process). Implement the checker as a pure function inside the test file (input: { readmeRows, tarballDigests, manifest, lock }, output: string[] of findings) so the same function runs against the real tree AND against in-memory negative fixtures: a README row with one hex digit changed -> finding naming the file and both digests; a `file:vendor/x.tgz` dependency absent from bundledDependencies -> finding; a lock entry with `inBundle: false` or a `resolved` that is not `file:vendor/<file>` -> finding; a tarball without a README row or without a package.json dependency -> orphan finding; a version in the filename that differs from the lock entry version -> finding.

Out of scope: changing vendor contents, versions, lockfile or package.json (if the real-tree run is red at rig HEAD, stop, record the mismatch in the ledger line and return blocked rather than editing pins); docs edits; src/ edits; forge.toml edits.

All criteria quote docs/workbench specs or vendor/README.md in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

1. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Current experimental distribution": "Native SDK artifacts are checksum-pinned and bundled so a packed parent can install them." -> for each of forge-sdk-0.1.0.tgz, furnace-sdk-0.1.0.tgz, hyperunix-sdk-0.1.0.tgz: sha256(bytes) equals the vendor/README.md table value; package.json dependencies contains `file:vendor/<file>` for the package; `bundledDependencies` includes the package; package-lock `packages["node_modules/<pkg>"]` has resolved === "file:vendor/<file>", inBundle === true, version equal to the version in the filename, and integrity matching /^sha(256|384|512)-[A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2}$/.
2. docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Supply chain": "Pin SDK versions, package/artifact digests and provenance." -> an in-memory fixture whose README digest differs by one hex digit yields a finding that names the file and both digests; a tarball with no README row, or no package.json dependency, yields an orphan finding; a filename/lock version disagreement yields a finding.
3. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Pin dependencies, lockfile and package exports." and docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md § "Clean external install": "npm could not resolve local native SDK tarballs before extracting the parent package." -> a fixture with a `file:vendor/` dependency absent from bundledDependencies, or whose lock entry has inBundle false, yields a finding; the test runs inside `npm run test` (portable gate) with no network and no npm child process.
4. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-048: "Artifact/host compatibility detects mismatched digest and rejects or explicitly migrates." -> the guard never auto-corrects: it only reports findings; nothing under vendor/ or package*.json is written (the test asserts those files' bytes are unchanged after the run).

They do not establish that the producing checkouts were clean or that every native runtime supports every SDK method." and docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Experimental immutable receipt": "Native executable identity remains a producer-specific observation." -> assertion messages and test names say the artifact BYTES are pinned and make no claim about native executables or clean producer checkouts.

title: VC-6/W17-A: pure digest-pinned workflow patch proposal (bounded redacted diff, static validation of the candidate, affected pinned invocations stay unchanged, operator-only promotion receipt; never writes source or replaces a running invocation); Pi tool registration excluded
description:

Human/operator promotes changes explicitly") for a CANDIDATE source. docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md lists WB-038, WB-039 and WB-047 as "planned" with no source or test. The VC-6 journey "Pi generates a source diff improving redundant task, validates it, executes reproducible comparison and cites native results" has no artifact between "generate a diff" and "validate".

src/workbench/patch-proposal.ts (new; imports only: type WorkflowSource, type WorkflowValidation, validateWorkflowSource from ./designer.js; type DefinitionRef, type InvocationSnapshot, canonicalJson, identityDigest from ./identity.js; type CapabilityRegistry from ./capability-registry.js; redactWorkbenchText from ./redaction.js; safeWorkflowTerminalText from ../ui/workflow-card.js; createHash from node:crypto. Nothing from node:fs, node:child_process or any provider):
• PATCH_PROPOSAL_CONTRACT = "workbench.patch-proposal/v1"; class PatchProposalError extends Error { code: "SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH" | "CANDIDATE_TOO_LARGE" | "PROMOTION_PRECONDITION" | "VALIDATION" }.
• proposeWorkflowPatch(input: { base: WorkflowSource; candidateSource: string; rationale: string; hypothesis?: { metric: string; direction: "lower" | "higher"; groundedIn: readonly string[] }; pinnedInvocations?: readonly InvocationSnapshot[]; registry?: CapabilityRegistry; grants?: readonly string[]; limits?: { maxDiffLines?: number; maxPreviewBytes?: number } }): WorkflowPatchProposal.
  – First check: base.definition.artifactDigest must equal `sha256:<hex>` of base.source (same form designer.ts uses) else throw PatchProposalError("SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH") before any diff or validation work.
  – candidate.definition = { ...base.definition, artifactDigest: sha256(candidateSource) }; validation = validateWorkflowSource({ definition: candidate.definition, sourceRef: base.sourceRef, source: candidateSource }, { registry, grants }) so SOURCE_TOO_LARGE, control-character, META and possible-call/grant diagnostics are inherited unchanged and `executed` stays false.
  – diff: deterministic line diff (LCS or Myers) over base vs candidate; hunks `{ op: "context" | "add" | "remove"; baseLine?: number; candidateLine?: number; text: string }` with text = safeWorkflowTerminalText(redactWorkbenchText(line)); bounded by limits.maxDiffLines (default 400) and limits.maxPreviewBytes (default 65536) with `truncated: boolean`; `summary: { added, removed, unchanged }` counted over the FULL diff even when the preview is truncated; identical bytes -> status "no-change" with zero hunks.
  – affectedPinnedInvocations: for each pinnedInvocations entry whose scriptDigest === base.definition.artifactDigest -> { logicalInvocationId, scriptDigest, action: "unchanged", note: "remains pinned to the base digest; the candidate requires a new logical invocation" }; other snapshots are only counted in unrelatedInvocations; input snapshots are never mutated.

description:
